Aaron Jamal Crawford was born on March 20, 1980.
Crawford is nicknamed "J-Crossover".
Crawford played for Rainier Beach High School.
Rainier Beach High retired Crawford's number 23 jersey.
Rainier Beach High inducted Crawford into its Hall of Fame.
Crawford committed to play college basketball with the University of Michigan under coach Brian Ellerbe.
The NCAA ruled that Crawford had breached amateurism bylaw during his high school years, resulting in a six-game suspension.
Crawford was selected 8th overall in the 2000 NBA draft by the Cleveland Cavaliers.
Cleveland Cavaliers traded Crawford to the Chicago Bulls.
In his first year as a Bull (2000–2001), Crawford struggled with his shot and converted only 35.2 percent from the field.
In his first year as a Bull, Crawford scored in double-digits 10 times.
Crawford averaged 4.6 points, 1.5 rebounds, and 2.3 assists across 61 games (8 starting) during his rookie season with the Bulls.

In his second NBA season (2001–2002), Crawford improved in nearly all statistical categories by averaging 9.3 points, 1.5 rebounds, and 2.4 assists while converting 44.8 percent of his attempts from behind the arc.
Crawford's third campaign with the Bulls (2002–2003) saw him emerge as a key component of coach Bill Cartwright's offense.
In his third season with the Bulls, Crawford averaged 10.7 points, 2.3 rebounds, 4.2 assists, and 1 steal across 80 games (31 starting).
The Bulls missed the playoffs in the 2002–2003 season with a 30–52 record.
Crawford's fourth NBA season (2003–2004) was his last in Chicago, where he averaged 17.3 points, 3.5 rebounds, and 5.1 assists per contest.
On April 11, 2004, Crawford scored 50 points against the Toronto Raptors in his third to last game as a Bull.
Crawford was traded from the Bulls to the New York Knicks along with Jerome Williams for Dikembe Mutombo, Othella Harrington, Frank Williams, and Cezary Trybanski.
In his first year with the Knicks (2004–2005), Crawford played 70 games (67 starting) and averaged 17.7 points, 2.9 rebounds, 4.3 assists, and 1.4 steals per contest.
Crawford had a notable win over the Charlotte Bobcats on December 4, 2004, where he scored 41 points on 17-of-25 shooting.
The Knicks fell short of the playoffs in the 2004–2005 season.

In his second year with the Knicks (2005–2006), Crawford took a reduced sixth man role under head coach Larry Brown and averaged 14.3 points, 3.1 rebounds, and 3.8 assists across 79 games (27 starting).
The Knicks had a record of 23–59 in the 2005–2006 season.

In 2006–2007, the Knicks replaced Larry Brown with Isiah Thomas as head coach and Crawford was limited to 59 games (36 starting) due to an ACL injury; he averaged 17.6 points, 3.2 rebounds, and 4.4 assists on the season.
In 2007–2008, Crawford played all 80 games in the starting lineup for the Knicks and averaged 20.6 points, 2.6 rebounds, and 5 assists.
On January 26, 2007, Crawford scored a career-high 52 points against the New York Knicks.
Crawford was traded to the Golden State Warriors along with Jerome Williams in exchange for Al Harrington.
In his first year with the Warriors (2008–2009), Crawford played in 54 games and started each one, averaging nearly 20 points per contest as well as 4.4 assists and 1.5 rebounds.
During a game against the Charlotte Bobcats on December 20, 2008, Crawford scored 50 points; thus he became the fourth player in NBA history to score 50+ points with three teams.
At the end of the season, the Atlanta Hawks acquired Crawford from the Warriors for guards Acie Law and Speedy Claxton.
Crawford joined the Atlanta Hawks for their 2009–10 season.
On January 15, 2010, Crawford made a three-point shot at the buzzer to clinch a 102–101 victory over the Phoenix Suns.
In a win over the Los Angeles Clippers on February 3, 2010, Crawford set an all-time NBA record for most career four-point plays, surpassing Reggie Miller.
Crawford averaged 18 points, 2.5 rebounds, and 2 assists off the bench in the 2009–10 season.
Crawford won the NBA Sixth Man of the Year Award in 2010.
The Hawks qualified for the playoffs with Crawford as a key player.
The Hawks advanced past the Milwaukee Bucks in seven games but were subsequently swept by the Orlando Magic.
Crawford led all scorers in game seven with 22 points.
In the 2010–11 season, the Hawks fired coach Mike Woodson to bring on Larry Drew.
Crawford had a solid season of averaging 14.2 points, 1.7 rebounds, and 3.2 assists per game in the 2010–11 season.
The Hawks made it to the playoffs as the 5th seed in the Eastern Conference.
In the opening round of the playoffs, the Hawks were defeated by the Orlando Magic in six games.
Crawford made the game-clinching three-pointer with six seconds left in Game 3 against the Orlando Magic.
The Hawks advanced to the conference semifinals but were eliminated by the Chicago Bulls in six games.
Crawford signed with the Portland Trail Blazers on December 15, 2011.
In the lockout-shortened season of 2011–2012, Crawford averaged nearly 14 points while leading the league in free throw percentage with a career-high 92.7 percent.
Crawford signed with the Los Angeles Clippers on July 11, 2012.
In the 2012–2013 season, Crawford posted 16.5 points, 1.7 rebounds, 2.5 assists, and 29.3 minutes in the 76 games he played.
Crawford finished second place in voting for the 2013 NBA Sixth Man of the Year Award.
In the opening round of the playoffs, the Clippers were defeated by the Memphis Grizzlies in six games.
During the playoffs that year, Crawford averaged 10.8 points, 2 rebounds, and 1.7 assists.
In the 2013–2014 season, Crawford led the league's reserve players in scoring with 18.6 points per contest to go along with 3.2 assists and 2.3 rebounds.
Crawford came off the bench in 45 of 69 games he played in during the 2013–2014 season.
On May 8, 2014, Crawford won the 2014 NBA Sixth Man of the Year Award for the second time.
Crawford helped the Clippers finish with their best record in franchise history (57–25) during the 2013–2014 season.
On December 8, 2014, Crawford received a technical and his first-ever ejection after getting tangled with Suns' guard Eric Bledsoe at midcourt.
During a game against the Phoenix Suns on November 2, 2015, Crawford scored 37 points in a 101–96 victory over the Detroit Pistons.
On January 10, 2016, Crawford recorded his 46th four-point play of his career in a 114–111 overtime win over the New Orleans Pelicans.
On April 8, 2016, Crawford made a three-pointer with 0.2 seconds left and finished with 30 points in the Clippers' 102–99 overtime victory over the Utah Jazz.
Crawford was named NBA Sixth Man of the Year for the third time in his career on April 19, 2016.
At 36 years old, Crawford broke his own record as the oldest winner of the award.
On December 2, 2016, Crawford passed Vince Carter (1,961) for No. 6 on the NBA's all-time list for made three-pointers with 1,962.

Crawford became the sixth NBA player to reach 2,000 made three-pointers by making a three-pointer at the 2:06 mark of the second quarter in the Clippers' 118–109 loss to the Toronto Raptors on February 6, 2017.
Crawford surpassed Eddie Johnson for No. 2 in career NBA bench scoring with his tally of 9,572 bench points trailing only Dell Curry's 11,147.
On February 11 against Charlotte, Crawford scored 22 points while shooting 5-of-8 on three-pointers.
Crawford passed Vince Carter (2,006) for fifth-most three-pointers made in NBA history with his tally of 2,009.

The Clippers traded Crawford and a 2018 first-round pick to the Atlanta Hawks as part of a salary dump that cleared the way to acquire Danilo Gallinari from the Denver Nuggets by a sign-and-trade deal on July 6, 2017.
Crawford was waived by the Hawks the following day after being traded.
On July 19, 2017, Crawford signed with the Minnesota Timberwolves.
During his debut for the Timberwolves (October 18, 2017), Crawford scored 10 points in a 107–99 loss to the San Antonio Spurs.

Two days later, during their home-opener, Crawford scored all 17 of his points in the fourth quarter and made a 3-pointer with 27.5 seconds left to help the Timberwolves hold off the Utah Jazz 100–97.
During a game against the Portland Trail Blazers on December 18, 2017, Crawford made a season-high 23 points in only 23 minutes, with 16 of them scored in the fourth quarter.
On March 30, 2018, during a win over the Dallas Mavericks, Crawford had a 24-point effort.
In June 2018, Crawford won the Twyman-Stokes Teammate of the Year Award.
Crawford signed with the Phoenix Suns on October 17, 2018.
During a game against the New York Knicks on December 17, 2018, Crawford dished out a career-high 14 assists.
On January 6, 2019, in a loss to the Charlotte Hornets, Crawford finished with 16 points and joined Dell Curry as the only NBA players to record 11,000+ career points as a reserve.
Per 36 minutes in the 2018–19 season, Crawford averaged 15.1 points to go along with a career-high of 6.8 assists.
Only John Stockton has averaged more assists per 36 minutes in their 19th or later season.
On April 9, 2019, during the season finale against the Dallas Mavericks, Crawford made NBA history by recording 51 points in his fourth 50-point game.

At 39 years old and 20 days, he broke two NBA records: the oldest player to tally 50+ points (held by Michael Jordan) and the most points scored by a player not in the starting lineup (held by Nick Anderson).
During the game, Crawford shot 18-of-30 from the field, 7-of-13 from three-point range, and 8-of-9 from the free-throw line.
He also had 5 rebounds, 5 assists, 1 steal, and 1 block coming off the bench.
Down by as much as 31 in the third quarter, Crawford rallied Phoenix back into the game, scoring 12 points in succession and bringing the score to 107–103 with 3:39 minutes left in the game.
By scoring 28 and 27 points in the previous two games, Crawford joined Kobe Bryant as the only players in league history to record three consecutive 25+ point games in their 19th season or later.
He also became the only player in NBA history to record 50 points in a game with four different teams.
On July 9, 2020, the Brooklyn Nets signed Crawford as a substitute player for the remainder of the 2019–20 season due to four players opting out of the NBA reboot in Orlando.
Crawford made his team debut on August 4, 2020, against the Milwaukee Bucks and became the oldest active player in the NBA at the time (40 years and 137 days old).
He also became the eighth player in NBA history to appear in a game in 20 different seasons.
Crawford recorded five points and three assists in five minutes before leaving the game with a left hamstring injury.
It was his only appearance for the Nets in their eight regular-season games and he did not play in their four playoff games.
His one appearance for the Nets was ultimately his final NBA game, as Crawford did not play for any team during the 2020–21 or 2021–22 seasons.
Crawford officially announced his retirement from the league on March 21, 2022.
Crawford started doing game broadcasts for NBA League Pass alongside Quentin Richardson in November 2021.
Crawford married his long-time girlfriend Tori Lucas on August 23, 2014.

Among those to attend Crawford's wedding were Clippers teammates Blake Griffin, Matt Barnes, Chris Paul, DeAndre Jordan, and Spencer Hawes; also in attendance were NBA players Nate Robinson and Isaiah Thomas.
Crawford organized secret workouts around the city of Seattle, recruiting a revolving cast of elite-level participants that included Zach LaVine and Kyrie Irving.
Crawford provided a platform for local players aspiring to progress from amateur status to professional through "The Crawsover" league at Seattle Pacific University.
This Pro–am summer-league is among the most prestigious in the country, yet admission is free.
Pros such as NBA All-Stars Chris Paul and Kevin Durant have participated in the past.
Crawford made a cameo in the music video for the song "Feelin Myself" by Seattle rapper, Kid Sensation.
